items.actClause:
AN ACT directing the department of public service to prepare a written report
on the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency on certain utilities (Part
A); and directing the department of environmental conservation to prepare a
written report on the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency on wastewater
utilities (Part B)
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5451

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act directing the department of public service to prepare a written
report on the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency on certain util-
ities (Part A); and directing the department of environmental conserva-
tion to prepare a written report on the effect of the COVID-19 state of
emergency on wastewater utilities (Part B)

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the legislation to conduct a comprehensive study of the
effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency on utilities and consumers

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Part A and Part requires the Public Service Commission and the Depart-
ment of Conservation, respectively, to study utilities response during
the COVID; accessing how many customers service are disconnected and how
many customers are behind on utility payment, and to what extent.

Part A and B: Within 30 days after the effective date, the Department of
Public Service and Department of Conservation, respectively, shall
prepare and submit to the governor and the legislature a written report.
An updated report shall be submitted monthly until 180 days after the
end of the COVID19 state of emergency and quarterly thereafter. The
Report shall include, amongst other things,(1) the number of customers
(2) disconnection notice sent due to non-payment (3)the number of liens
on real property placed, sold or enforced due to non-payment (4) the
numbers of customers in arrears,(5) the number of customers that became
eligible for disconnection, and (6) the number of customer enrolled in
deferred payment agreement.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The COVID-19 pandemic has undoubtedly placed pressure on essential
public services, including utility services. Public utilities, including
municipally owned, were required to continue operation during the
pandemic; utilities were required to continue providing service to
consumers notwithstanding nonpayment of customers. The passage of a
utility moratorium in New York was essential, has proper sanitation was,
and is, a crucial fight against the spread of the COVID-19 virus. Howev-
er, there remains an existing financial impact for both customers and
utility companies that needs to be studied so that we can formulate an
adequate legislative response.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5451A

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act directing the department of public service to prepare a written
report on the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency on certain util-
ities (Part A); and directing the department of environmental conserva-
tion to prepare a written report on the effect of the COVID-19 state of
emergency on wastewater utilities (Part B)

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The purpose of the legislation is to conduct a comprehensive study of
the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency, on utilities and consum-
ers.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Part A and Part B requires the Department of Public Service to study
utilities' collections, customer activity and other financial impacts
during the COVID-19 State of Emergency and thereafter; reporting upon
how many customers' service are disconnected and reconnected, how many
customers are behind on utility payment (i.e., in arrears), and to what
extent such debt is"uncollectible" and burdens affordability.

Part A and B: Within 60 days after the effective date, the Department of
Public Service shall prepare and submit to the governor and the legisla-
ture a written report. An updated report shall be submitted monthly
until 180 days after the end of the COVID-19 state of emergency, and
quarterly thereafter until the covered entity ceases to provide service
in the state. The Report shall include, amongst other things, (1) the
number of customer disconnection notices sent due to non-payment (2)the
number of liens on real property placed, sold or enforced due to nonpay-
ment (3) the numbers of customers in arrears,(4) the number of customers
that became eligible for disconnection, and (5) the number of customer
enrolled in deferred payment agreements; (6)the amount of debt, and such
other collections and financial data necessary for formulation of
evidence-based policy.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

By the end of year one of the COVID-19 pandemic (e.g., February 2020 to
March 2021, more than 1.4 million households owed energy utilities in
excess of $1.5 billion- a number has increased further today.  Little is
known concerning debt to non-energy utilities because the State of New
York has not collected such data prior to this legislation. This massive
arrears crisis has undoubtedly placed pressure on essential public
services, including utility services, and could hold back economic
recovery in large areas of the State. Public utilities, including muni-
cipally-owned utilities, were required to continue operation during the
pandemic irrespective of their customers' inability to pay their bills
in part or full. All utilities, including municipal and public authority
utilities, were required to continue providing service to consumers
notwithstanding nonpayment, and were forbidden to terminate service or
engage in normal collections activity. The passage of a utility morato-
rium in New York was essential, as proper sanitation was, and is, a
crucial weapon in the fight against the spread of the COVID49 virus.
However, there remains an existing financial impact for both customers
and utility companies that must be studied to provide evidence necessary
for an adequate legislative response to assist New York's economy to
grow its way out of the COVID-1 9 Recession.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

To be determined

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

C.actClause:
AN ACT directing the department of public service to prepare a written report
on the affordability of utility services
C.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5451C

SPONSOR: PARKER
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act directing the department of public service to prepare a written
report on the affordability of utility services

 
PURPOSE OF BILL:

The purpose of the legislation is to conduct a comprehensive study of
the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency, on utilities and consum-
ers.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 lays out the definitions applicable to this act.

Section 2 requires utilities to submit data regarding arrears and
affordability to the PSC for the PSC to produce an initial report and an
updated report on the effect of the COVID-19 state of emergency on
arrears and affordability of utility services in New York State.

Section 3 allows utilities and municipalities to petition the PSC if
they believe the data required to be submitted to the PSC by this act
cannot be reasonably obtained without an increase in customer utility
bills.

Section 4 requires the PSC to publish the reports required pursuant to
section 2 of this act to its website simultaneously with the submission
of each report to the governor and legislature.

Section 5 is the severability clause.

Section 6 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

By the end of year one of the COVID-19 pandemic (e.g., February 2020 to
March 2021), more than 1.4 million households owed energy utilities in
excess of $1.5 billion- a number has increased further today. Little is
known concerning debt to non-energy utilities because the State of New

EFFECTIVE DATE:

VETO MESSAGE - No. 73
 
TO THE ASSEMBLY:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:
 
Assembly Bill Number 340-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public authorities law, in relation to direct-
      ing the New York state energy research and  development  authority
      to prepare a report regarding the replacement of decommissioned or
      dormant  electric  generating sites with renewable energy develop-
      ment and energy storage opportunities"
 
Assembly Bill Number 658-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to establishing
      the problem gambling advisory council"
 
Assembly Bill Number 2185-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to establishing a dyslexia and  dysgraphia  task
      force"

Assembly Bill Number 4117, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the environmental conservation law, in relation to
      declaring the goal of the state of  New  York  to  source  reduce,
      reuse, recycle, or compost no less than eighty-five percent of the
      solid waste generated by the year 2032"
 
Assembly Bill Number 4535-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the insurance law, in relation to commuter van and
      ambulette or paratransit vehicles classification review"
 
Assembly Bill Number 4908, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to establish a task force  to  identify  evidence-based  and
      evidence  informed  solutions  to  reduce  children's  exposure to
      adverse childhood experience"
 
Assembly Bill Number 5557, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to establish a commission to  be  known  as  the  "New  York
      seawall study commission"
 
Assembly Bill Number 6430-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to creating the
      sickle cell disease detection and education program"
 
Assembly Bill Number 6710-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing  the
      commission  of  the  deaf, deafblind and hard of hearing; to amend
      the social services law, in relation to requiring  the  commission
      of the deaf, deafblind, and hard of hearing to transmit complaints
 
      in  matters  affective  the  deaf,  deafblind, and hard of hearing
      communities to the vulnerable persons' central  register;  and  to
      repeal  section  559 of the executive law relating to the New York
      state interagency coordinating council for services to persons who
      are deaf, deaf-blind, or hard of hearing"
 
Assembly Bill Number 7230-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing
      the primary care reform commission"
 
Assembly Bill Number 7357-A, entitled:

    "AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to establishing
      a pilot program to create an assistance  hotline  for  individuals
      with  intellectual  and  developmental  disabilities  and  complex
      behavioral needs"
 
Assembly Bill Number 8418-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to require the New York state energy research  and  develop-
      ment authority to develop recommendations regarding the establish-
      ment of microgrids"
 
Assembly Bill Number 8881-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing
      the office of hospice and palliative care access and quality"
 
Assembly Bill Number 9080-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to a study of the number of children  in  foster
      care who have a developmental disability"
 
Assembly Bill Number 9275, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to establishing the New York state cryptocurren-
      cy  and  blockchain study task force; and providing for the repeal
      of such provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
Assembly Bill Number 9298-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to authorize and direct the commissioner of health to estab-
      lish a portable diagnostics program"
 
Assembly Bill Number 9348, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to establishing the fentanyl abuse and  overdose
      prevention  task  force;  and  providing  for  the  repeal of such
      provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
Assembly Bill Number 9448-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to requiring the commissioner  of  taxation  and
      finance to study the frequency of residents who are being assessed
      library  taxes  for  more than one library and to make recommenda-
      tions to prevent the double taxation of residents;  and  providing
      for the repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
Assembly Bill Number 9710, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  in  relation  to  conducting a study of public and private
      museums in New York state"

Assembly Bill Number 10139, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to establishing a temporary commission to  study
      aging  in  place  in  mental health housing; and providing for the
      repeal of such provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
Assembly Bill Number 10189, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to direct the department of civil service to  study  certain
      airport-related titles"
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bills:
 
Senate Bill Number 334-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to reports on
      short term crisis respite and intensive crisis respite programs"
 
Senate Bill Number 410-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to establish a Minority Coordinating  Council  on  Asthmatic
      Affairs"
 
Senate Bill Number 555-C, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to amend the elder law, in relation to creating the office
      of older adult workforce development within  the  office  for  the
      aging"

Senate Bill Number 774-B, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the executive law, in relation to requiring the
      collection of certain demographic  information  by  certain  state
      agencies, boards and commissions"
 
Senate Bill Number 5031, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the parks, recreation and historic preservation
      law, in relation to establishing the state parks passport program"
 
Senate Bill Number 5451-C, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT directing the department of  public  service  to  prepare  a
      written report on the affordability of utility services"
 
Senate Bill Number 5676, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to a review and
      recommendations of reimbursement adequacy and other matters relat-
      ing to early intervention"
 
Senate Bill Number 5734-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  requiring a multi-agency study on the issues impacting the
      continuum of caregiving in the state of New York"

Senate Bill Number 6208-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the parks,  recreation  and  historic  preservation
      law,  in relation to the development and posting of a senior trail
      guide that identifies walking and hiking opportunities for  active
      seniors  within  the state park system and along public non-motor-
      ized multi-use trails within the state"
 
Senate Bill Number 6501-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing  the
      LGBTQ+ advisory board"
 
Senate Bill Number 7377, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the mental hygiene law, in relation to establishing
      the statewide group home families working group"
 
Senate Bill Number 7429, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT directing the commissioner of labor to conduct a comprehen-
      sive study on immigrant and refugee participation in adult  educa-
      tion  and  the  workforce;  and  providing  for the repeal of such
      provisions upon expiration thereof"

Senate Bill Number 7752, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT directing the commissioner of mental health to  establish  a
      maternal  mental  health  workgroup to study and issue recommenda-
      tions related to maternal mental health and perinatal and postpar-
      tum mood and anxiety disorders; and providing for  the  repeal  of
      such provision upon expiration thereof"
 
Senate Bill Number 8231-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend  the executive law, in relation to requiring the
      office of children and family services to submit an annual  report
      about juvenile recidivism and cost of juvenile incarceration"
 
Senate Bill Number 9019, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT in relation to establishing a Caumsett State Park fire read-
      iness study"
 
Senate Bill Number 9086, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT relating to assessing the staffing and other issues causing
      the continued displacement of individuals with developmental disa-
      bilities from various state-operated institutions under the juris-
      diction of the office for people with developmental disabilities"
 
Senate Bill Number 9177-B, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the executive law, in relation to establishing  the
      New York Asian American and Pacific Islander commission"
 
Senate Bill Number 9462, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  establishing  the  special joint legislative commission on
      affordable  housing;  and  providing  for  the  repeal   of   such
      provisions upon expiration thereof"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  These  thirty-nine  bills would establish various commissions and task
forces touching nearly every aspect of state government. Several of  the
bills  would  require  intensive studies and reports to be undertaken by
state agencies and authorities. I share a strong interest in  addressing
the  problems  and  issues identified in this legislation, and I commend
the Legislature for seeking to address such a broad array of problems.
 
  However, enactment of this package of legislation  would  collectively
cost  the State approximately forty million dollars. None of these costs
are accounted for in the State Financial Plan. Without appropriate fund-
ing, these unbudgeted costs would create significant staffing and  other
programmatic  burdens  on  state  agencies. Additionally, because of the
ongoing work  of  state  agencies  and  authorities,  a  number  of  the
proposals would result in duplication and unnecessary bureaucracy.
 
  Many  of  the proposed studies, task forces and commissions are impor-
tant to a wide-variety of stake holders and constituencies. Therefore, I
am directing state agencies that have ongoing efforts or future plans to
address the issues described in these bills to  continue  their  efforts
and to review and incorporate the goals in the legislation to the extent
practicable.  Where  this  is  not the case, I am directing my office to
work with state agencies to assess what components  of  the  legislation
can be implemented using resources already in their financial plans.
 
  Because  of the fiscal impact of this legislation, the proposals would
be more appropriately considered in the  context  of  the  State  budget
process.  Therefore, I am constrained to veto these bills.
 
  These bills are disapproved.                   (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
